title: Walls, not algebra, decide which three-place contacts are rigid in direction
subject: Which contacts of twisted fair worlds contradict along all odd classes or none, and why the others select
conclusion: At three places, rigidity in direction is decided by the geometry of walls, not by algebra: all three-place tiling contacts have trivial polymorphisms, and renaming the places of one relation can change its kind. Contacts with free stripes or straight pinned walls are rigid on every torus, with an exact count; the twelve whose walls can turn are selective, and when their walls have no choices a direction contradicts exactly where every wall collides with its own copy.
